title: A real Linux, in your browser
question: This page runs Linux itself. What happens when a program asks it something?
text: This page runs a real Linux kernel, compiled for the browser. The program below made one syscall, `umask(077)`: it asks the kernel to set the mask that new files take their permissions from. The kernel answered 18, the mask before.

The kernel recorded everything it did for that call. Above: the timeline, a bar for each function it ran. Below it: the source, at the line the [cursor](1:__wasm_sys_umask) is on. On the right: the Stack, the calls that led there, with their values.
Now change the program: click its line, write another value, `umask(0)`, and press Enter. The kernel starts again and runs yours. Or try:
[twice](try:1): the second call returns what the first set (077, which is 63). [a mask too big](try:2): the kernel keeps only the permission bits, 0777.
